newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers firm in Mideast on tight tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers firm in Mideast on tight tonnage.

text.p: Clean tanker rates firmed this week in the Middle East due to tight tonnage availability and strong Indian demand, brokers said on Friday.
"Clean tanker rates have made significant gains with the Indians heading into the market for loadings early in the month.
"They been taking a lot of diesel and kerosene from Kuwait and Bahrain," one broker said, adding that strong East Asian demand had also led to a shortage of vessels in the Middle East.

E.A. Gibson said in their weekly tanker report that one charterer had to fix 33,000 tonnes for a voyage from the Middle East Gulf to India at W390 for early January loading. This compares with around W250 reported in mid-December.
"The lack of tonnage combined with some charterers still needing to cover cargoes should allow those owners with vessels in position to enjoy the new year...
"(Clean) Freight levels are expected to remain steady for the remainder of the month,...due to a dearth of tonnage in the area," Gibson added.
In the U.K./Cont the Pablo Neruda was fixed at W245 for Glencore with 33,000 tonnes of gasoline to the U.S. Gulf on Jan 13 -- a typical rate for transatlantic trips, brokers said.
In the Med the Seaempress II was fixed at W195 for Petrofina for a Sicily/Med trip on Jan 6.

An Italian broker said the market was picking up in the Med. "On the clean side things have been going up in the last 10 days. There are not so many vessels and many are employed on owners' programmes or charters," he added.
He said over W200 had been reported for 25,000 tonnes of naphtha on a Greece-Brindisi trip.
In the Caribs sector the Nordfast with 28,500 tonnes of unleaded gasoline at a lumpsum of $212,500 for Maraven was representative of the market, brokers said.
